Introduction
Tuberculosis remains a major cause of infectious disease mortality globally, accounting for an estimated 1.23 million deaths in 2024 [1]. Achieving progress in reducing this burden depends critically on maintaining high rates of completion of curative therapy. Despite the availability of effective drug regimens for decades, many high-burden countries have struggled to translate the high cure rates observed in clinical trials and controlled settings into everyday practice [2]. Mortality trends in WHO Region of the Americas further highlight this challenge, with limited progress overall and increasing mortality in several countries, including Brazil, since 2015 [1].
Loss to follow-up (LTFU) over the standard 6 months of tuberculosis treatment represents an important programmatic gap in tuberculosis care and a major contributor to adverse outcomes. When LTFU occurs, consequences include Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance, ongoing transmission, and increased mortality [1]. However, quantifying these effects presents several challenges. LTFU is not a random event, and a range of demographic and clinical characteristics have been associated with increased risk, including male sex, younger age, lower educational attainment, HIV co-infection, prior tuberculosis, and substance use [1,2].
Estimating the impact of LTFU on mortality is therefore complicated by confounding, as factors influencing disengagement from care also affect subsequent outcomes [3]. These effects can act in multiple directions: individuals with greater social vulnerabilities may be more likely to interrupt treatment and have poor outcomes, while individuals with more severe disease, who are at greatest risk of death, might be less likely to discontinue therapy than those with less advanced disease and few symptoms.
Comparisons between individuals who interrupt treatment and those who complete it are also subject to several distinct forms of immortal-time bias [4]. When exposure is assigned at treatment initiation according to how treatment later ended, individuals are classified as LTFU on the basis of an event that occurs only after part of their treatment has been survived: anyone who dies before disengaging is recorded as an on-treatment death and can only appear in the comparison group. The time from treatment initiation to disengagement, which may occur at any point during treatment, is therefore immortal-time for the LTFU group, and counting it as exposed biases the comparison toward a protective effect of LTFU [5]. Furthermore, because programmatic LTFU is declared only after a specified period of absence, incorrectly attributing that interval to the LTFU group can introduce additional immortal-time bias. Conversely, defining the comparator as individuals who complete therapy introduces immortal-time bias from the other direction, since treatment completion is itself a post-baseline outcome attainable only by surviving to the end of treatment.
Prior studies have consistently found higher mortality after LTFU [6–11], but most compared individuals lost to follow-up with those recorded as cured or as having completed treatment [6,7,9,11], a group that necessarily survived to treatment completion, thereby conditioning the comparison on survival. None has systematically addressed the immortal-time biases described above, so the magnitude of the excess mortality caused by disengagement remains unknown. Quantifying the effects of LTFU on mortality and identifying the groups at greatest risk of harm from LTFU are both important for prioritizing resources and developing effective strategies to address this problem.
We therefore aimed to address these methodological challenges and estimate the effect of LTFU on mortality, under explicitly stated identification assumptions, using a large population-based cohort linking tuberculosis surveillance and mortality data over long-term follow-up. We set out to answer three questions: how much excess mortality is attributable to disengagement; whether that effect depends on when during therapy disengagement occurs; and in which populations the absolute excess is largest. We additionally examined the causes of death underlying the excess to assess whether it is consistent with a causal pathway through interrupted therapy.
Methods
Study design and data sources
We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from TBweb, the electronic tuberculosis surveillance system of the São Paulo State Tuberculosis Program, and the Brazilian Mortality Information System (SIM). TBweb is an electronic surveillance platform used to notify and monitor all individuals diagnosed with tuberculosis in São Paulo State. The system is integrated with the national Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN), and uses the SINAN identification number as a unique person-level identifier, enabling longitudinal follow-up and linkage of multiple tuberculosis episodes for the same individual. SIM is Brazil’s national mortality registry, which records all deaths nationwide. Death certificates follow the international format, and the underlying cause of death is assigned by trained coders based on the reported sequence of conditions. The quality of SIM has recently been evaluated: registration completeness has improved over time and the proportion of deaths assigned an ill-defined or otherwise uninformative underlying cause fell substantially between 2000 and 2015, with the remaining shortfalls concentrated in the North and Northeast rather than in São Paulo State [12,13]. The study extract included the underlying cause of death; the contributing conditions recorded on the remaining lines of the certificate were available from the same linkage and were used in a secondary analysis. TBweb and SIM records were probabilistically linked to identify deaths during follow-up (Section B in S1 Appendix). The study included all tuberculosis notifications recorded in TBweb between January 1, 2013, and December 31, 2023, with administrative censoring on December 31, 2024 to allow at least 1-year of follow-up. Data extraction and linkage were performed in January 2025. No prospective protocol or statistical analysis plan was published or registered; the analyses that were planned, and the changes made during the study and in response to peer review, are described under Changes to the analysis. This study is reported as per the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guideline (S1 Checklist) and, for the target trial emulation, as per the TrAnsparent ReportinG of studies Emulating a Target trial (TARGET) guideline (S2 Checklist); the specification and emulation of the target trial protocol are reported in Table E in S1 Appendix.
Study population
The study cohort included individuals aged 15 years or older at the time of their first new tuberculosis notification in São Paulo State, Brazil, between 2013 and 2023. Each individual contributed a single episode: their earliest new-case notification, excluding notifications later reclassified as not tuberculosis or lacking a recorded treatment outcome. Whether that episode ended in LTFU defined the exposure. We excluded individuals with missing or implausible dates (e.g., death occurring before treatment initiation date), administrative transfers outside São Paulo State or Brazil, or no recorded treatment start date. Later notifications did not contribute to exposure, but were used to ascertain cause of death. All counts refer to individuals, not notifications.
Exposures and outcomes
LTFU during the first tuberculosis episode was the exposure of interest. Under Brazilian national guidelines, LTFU is defined as treatment interruption for at least 30 consecutive days [14]. Therefore, the date recorded in the registry is the LTFU declaration date: the first day on which LTFU can be classified, after the individual has gone at least 30 days without documented medication use. To approximate the date on which treatment was actually interrupted, we defined the interruption date as 30 days before the declaration date. Where each date enters the analysis differs between the two designs and is specified below.
Death was ascertained using two data sources. First, deaths were identified within TBweb based on-treatment outcomes recorded. Second, deaths were identified through probabilistic linkage with SIM, as described in section B in S1 Appendix. When date-of-death discrepancies between sources were identified, records were verified for individual identity and administrative consistency, and the earliest recorded date of death was used. Outcomes were classified as tuberculosis-attributable deaths and nontuberculosis deaths. Tuberculosis-attributable deaths were defined using ICD-10 codes for underlying causes from SIM, supplemented by TBweb case-closure classifications. SIM records an underlying cause, defined as the condition that initiated the sequence of events leading to death, together with the contributing conditions entered on the remaining certificate lines. Deaths were counted as tuberculosis-attributable only where tuberculosis was the underlying cause; we repeated the cause attribution counting tuberculosis recorded on any line as a secondary analysis (Section C.4 in S1 Appendix). Nontuberculosis deaths were defined as all other causes.
Covariates for all models were age group, sex, race, education, HIV status, diabetes, alcohol use, drug use, incarceration, homelessness, hospitalization at diagnosis, clinical tuberculosis classification, directly observed therapy (DOT), and municipality of treatment classified according to the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) rural–urban typology [15], custody settings being folded into the urban reference level because that category is collinear with incarceration. All were defined at the time of treatment initiation, as TBweb records these characteristics at notification and does not reliably update them during treatment. Hospitalization at diagnosis is not routine in Brazil: the main indications are clinical severity, management of comorbidity including advanced HIV disease, and social circumstances in which outpatient treatment is not feasible. DOT is the practice of a person watching the patient take their tuberculosis medication in real time, and forms part of the broader strategy promoted by the World Health Organization to support adherence to treatment. DOT is recommended for everyone treated for tuberculosis in Brazil but is not always achievable, for example where an individual lives far from the treating facility, where work schedules conflict with daily observation, or where housing is unstable.
Statistical analysis
Multiple imputation.
Missing data were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations with random-forest predictors, assuming the data were missing at random [16]. The imputation model included all baseline covariates, the exposure, event indicators, and follow-up times, along with three predictors of missingness not in the adjustment set: calendar year of treatment start, recorded mental health condition, and setting of diagnosis. Missingness was related to recorded characteristics, most strongly to calendar year of treatment start and, for education, to social circumstances. The imputation model therefore conditioned on these, along with the complete outcome and follow-up time (Section D.1 in S1 Appendix). Imputation was applied to covariates only. We generated five imputed datasets. Multivariable analyses were fitted separately in each imputed dataset and pooled using Rubin’s rules. Complete-case analyses were conducted as sensitivity analyses (Section D.2 in in S1 Appendix).
Causal analyses: Target trial emulation and rolling landmark
The primary analysis emulated a target trial from the start of treatment [17,18], contrasting two strategies: disengagement from treatment at any point during the first six months, and remaining engaged throughout that window. Because an individual’s future disengagement cannot be known at treatment start, each individual was cloned into both strategies. Each clone was censored at the point at which the observed history diverged from its assigned strategy (for the continued engagement strategy, the recorded LTFU declaration date) and the resulting informative censoring was corrected with inverse-probability-of-censoring weights [19] estimated from the covariates listed above together with a municipality random intercept. An individual who was alive and still engaged within the window was compatible with both strategies, so deaths occurring at that time point contributed to both arms; surviving to the point of disengagement was not a condition of entering the analysis. Standardized cumulative mortality risk was computed under each strategy and contrasted at 60 months as a risk difference and a risk ratio. Follow-up was not extended beyond 60 months because the proportion of the cohort with sufficient follow-up declines steeply thereafter. Confidence intervals were obtained from a bootstrap that resamples municipalities, to allow for nonindependence of individuals treated in the same municipality; because São Paulo city contributes one third of the cohort, it was included in every replicate with its individuals resampled, and the remaining 639 municipalities were resampled as whole clusters (Section I in in S1 Appendix).
The timing of disengagement was addressed with a separate rolling landmark design [20]. One landmark trial was opened for each day on which any individual was declared LTFU: individuals declared on that day formed the exposed arm, individuals still in care on that day formed the comparator, and follow-up for both arms began on that day. The 30-day grace period required by the LTFU definition therefore applies symmetrically, since both arms must be alive and event-free at the landmark. Trials were stacked and fitted with a single Cox model adjusted for the covariates listed above and a municipality random intercept, and absolute risks were obtained by g-formula standardization [21] to the disengaging population. Confidence intervals for the landmark risk differences were obtained with the same municipality-resampling bootstrap as the target trial emulation, rebuilding the stacked trials in each replicate; hazard ratios reported in sensitivity analyses use standard errors clustered on individual, because individuals contribute to more than one trial (Section I in S1 Appendix). Because the proportional-hazards assumption was rejected over a five-year horizon, the exposure was given a separate coefficient in each of five disjoint follow-up periods and the cumulative hazard assembled piecewise, so that the standardized risks do not assume a constant hazard ratio.
The two designs use different time origins (treatment start for the target trial emulation, the individual’s own declaration date for the landmark) and their magnitudes are therefore not comparable. The landmark exposed arm is smaller than the cohort total lost to follow-up because exposure must be indexed on a day of disengagement within the treatment course (Section A in S1 Appendix). Both were repeated within subgroups defined by age group, sex, HIV status, homelessness, drug resistance, and calendar period of treatment initiation. The two designs, and the time origin each uses, are shown in Fig 1. Both designs identify a causal effect only under assumptions the data cannot verify: that the arms are exchangeable conditional on the measured baseline covariates, so that no unmeasured determinant of both disengagement and death remains; that censoring at divergence from an assigned strategy is uninformative given those covariates and the weight model; and that both strategies were possible for every individual at the time origin. Unmeasured severity is the assumption most likely to fail, and Section F in S1 Appendix quantifies how strong such a confounder would need to be to explain the estimate away.

Cause-specific analyses
To assess whether the association between LTFU and mortality is consistent with the effects of treatment interruption or reflects residual confounding, we repeated the rolling landmark cohort analysis using cause-specific mortality outcomes, evaluating deaths due to tuberculosis and other causes. We utilized this design as the question concerns deaths after LTFU, whereas the target trial emulation shares deaths occurring before the two strategies diverge and dilutes the cause-specific contrast. Cause-specific Cox models were fitted by censoring deaths from the alternate cause at the time of occurrence. Cumulative incidence functions were then constructed (Aalen–Johansen) so that the tuberculosis and nontuberculosis components sum to the all-cause risk difference. Deaths whose cause could not be classified were included in the nontuberculosis class.
Sensitivity analyses
We conducted sensitivity analyses to assess the robustness of the primary findings. First, cause-specific analyses were restricted to deaths with an ICD-10 classification from SIM only (Section C.2 in S1 Appendix), and were repeated counting tuberculosis recorded on any line of the death certificate rather than only as the underlying cause (Section C.4 in in S1 Appendix). Second, analyses were stratified by calendar period (Section E in S1 Appendix). Third, we repeated the primary rolling landmark cohort analysis in the complete-case set, restricted to individuals with complete data for all covariates (Section D.2 in S1 Appendix). Fourth, we quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding by computing an E-value for the primary risk ratio, which gives the minimum strength of association an unmeasured confounder would need with both disengagement and mortality to explain the estimate away (Section F in S1 Appendix). Fifth, we repeated the primary analysis without the municipality random intercept, and with confidence intervals obtained by resampling individuals or by resampling all municipalities as clusters (Section I in S1 Appendix). In addition, we conducted descriptive supplementary analyses of temporal trends in LTFU incidence and post-LTFU outcomes across the study period. Finally, to evaluate how much of the variation in published estimates reflects study design rather than the underlying association, we applied the design used by most prior studies to this cohort, with follow-up from treatment initiation and a comparator of individuals recorded as cured, holding the covariates and horizon fixed. Because prior studies report relative measures, that comparison is made on the hazard ratio scale.
Changes to the analysis
The study questions, cohort definition, and exposure and outcome definitions were established before analysis. Several analytical decisions were made during the study rather than pre-specified. The 60-month follow-up horizon was selected based on the availability of follow-up data, and a period-flexible model was adopted after the proportional-hazards assumption was rejected.
The analytical approach was also refined in response to peer review. The original fixed-month landmark analysis was replaced with a rolling landmark design anchored at each individual’s LTFU declaration date to address immortal-time bias, and the target trial emulation became the primary analysis. We also added a municipality random intercept to the censoring model of the target trial emulation to address geographic clustering.

Results
Study population
TBweb recorded 235,629 individuals with tuberculosis between 2013 and 2023, of whom 219,282 had a first tuberculosis episode. Of these, 6,552 were excluded due to a change of diagnosis, 12,460 due to missing or incomplete outcome information, and 1,861 due to transfer during treatment to another state or country. Further exclusions included individuals aged <15 years (n = 6,178) and deaths recorded on or before treatment initiation (n = 549). Episodes with recorded outcome dates outside the study period (2013–2023) were also excluded (n = 17,834), and 21 individuals whose tuberculosis was identified only post-mortem were excluded as never at risk for LTFU. Finally, 2,779 cases with missing or inconsistent treatment dates (800 LTFU, 1,979 continued-in-care) were excluded from the primary analysis to ensure consistent time-on-treatment alignment. The final primary cohort comprised 171,048 individuals (Fig 2), 97.2% of the 175,998 adults with a first tuberculosis episode ending within the study period. Of these, 20,830 (12.2%) experienced LTFU during their first episode. Among individuals who were not LTFU, 135,699 (90.3%) were programmatically classified as cured, 12,336 (8.2%) as deaths (5,520 tuberculosis-related and 6,816 nontuberculosis-related), 1,044 (0.7%) as treatment failure, and 1,139 (0.8%) as other outcomes, including regimen changes due to toxicity.

Compared with individuals who continued in care, those who were LTFU were younger (median age 33 years, interquartile range [IQR] 25–42, versus 37, IQR 27–51), more frequently male (78.7% versus 70.4%), and reported higher prevalence of homelessness (10.6% versus 2.3%), alcohol use (29.9% versus 16.2%), drug use (35.6% versus 13.9%), and HIV (11.4% versus 7.6%). They were also more often hospitalized at diagnosis (32.9% versus 23.6%) and less likely to receive DOT (65.4% versus 74.4%). (Table 1)
Annual LTFU risk rose from approximately 10% in 2013–2018 to ~15% in 2021–2022, coinciding with the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Drug-susceptibility testing (DST) yielded a conclusive result in 21.7% of the cohort (n = 37,190/171,048). Among those tested, 1.51% (n = 562) had rifampin-resistant or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis and 2.25% (n = 836) had isoniazid mono-resistant disease. LTFU rates were broadly similar across drug resistance categories: 11.7% (95% CI [9.3, 14.7]) among individuals with rifampin- or multidrug-resistant TB, 13.5% (95% CI [13.1, 13.9]) in the drug-sensitive group, and 11.8% (95% CI [11.7, 12.0]) among those without a recorded DST result. LTFU was declared at a median of 3.88 months (IQR [2.11, 5.43]) from treatment start, and at a median of 3.12 months among the 17,150 declared within the first six months (Fig 3A).

Mortality after LTFU
Among the 20,830 individuals who experienced LTFU, 9,395 (45.1%) subsequently began a retreatment episode, 453 (2.2%) died without returning to treatment, and 10,982 (52.7%) had no further recorded episode (Fig 3D). Among those who returned, 4,010 (42.7%) were cured, and 4,307 (45.8%) were again LTFU. Post-LTFU observation totaled 111,703 person-years, with a median of 5.0 years (IQR [2.5, 8.0]) per individual; 1,668 (8.0%) died, at a median of 17.5 months (IQR [6.7, 38.9]) after LTFU, a crude mortality rate of 14.9 deaths per 1,000 person-years (95% CI [14.2, 15.7]).
Crude five-year mortality after LTFU varied more than 5-fold across baseline characteristics (Fig 4): 20.0% among people living with HIV (PLHIV) compared with 6.3% among HIV–negative individuals; 17.5% among individuals hospitalized at diagnosis versus 3.0% among those who were not; 14.5% among individuals experiencing homelessness compared with 7.1% among housed individuals; 11.0% among those reporting alcohol use versus 6.6% among those not; and rising with age from 4.4% at 15–24 years to 16.4% at 65 years or above. Cause-specific evidence: TB-attributable versus non-TB mortality
A cause of death was available from either source for 86.4% of deaths within 5 years in the exposed arm and 88.1% in the comparator arm. A cause coded in the national mortality registry was available for 37.2% and 41.9%, respectively; the remainder was taken from the programmatic outcome recorded in TBweb. When both sources cited the same cause of death (n = 2,618), they agreed on tuberculosis versus nontuberculosis attribution in 76.2% of cases (Cohen's κ = 0.52).
The excess was concentrated in deaths attributed to tuberculosis. On the absolute scale, the 5-year excess of 2.68 percentage points (95% CI [2.28, 3.24]) was partitioned into 1.64 percentage points attributed to tuberculosis (95% CI [1.28, 1.93]) and 1.04 percentage points not attributed to tuberculosis (95% CI [0.80, 1.49]). Tuberculosis therefore accounted for 61% of the total excess. Restricting cause of death to ICD-10 codes recorded in the mortality registry gave the same ordering (Section C.2 in S1 Appendix). Counting tuberculosis recorded on any line of the death certificate rather than only as the underlying cause classified 26% more deaths as tuberculosis-related and raised the tuberculosis share of the excess from 61% to 63% (1.68 versus 1.64 percentage points), with the reclassified deaths falling in both arms (Section C.4 in S1 Appendix).
Effect modification of LTFU
Effects were compared across subgroups within the same target trial emulation, at 60 months (Fig 6A and 6B). On the relative scale, the risk ratio was highest in the youngest individuals (15–24 years, 1.90, 95% CI [1.67, 2.16]) and declined with age, to 1.42 (95% CI [1.37, 1.52]) at 25–44 years, 1.23 (95% CI [1.16, 1.30]) at 45–64 years, and 1.07 (95% CI [0.99, 1.15]) at 65 years or above. PLHIV had a lower risk ratio (1.20, 95% CI [1.14, 1.25]) than HIV–negative individuals (1.27, 95% CI [1.23, 1.33]), and individuals experiencing homelessness had a lower ratio (1.09, 95% CI [1.01, 1.17]) than housed persons (1.27, 95% CI [1.24, 1.32]). Estimates were similar by sex (female 1.28, 95% CI [1.20, 1.39]; male 1.25, 95% CI [1.21, 1.30]) and across calendar periods (2013–2019: 1.28, 95% CI [1.23, 1.33]; 2020–2023: 1.26, 95% CI [1.19, 1.36]).
On the absolute scale the ordering reverses. The 60-month risk difference was largest among PLHIV (5.16 percentage points, 95% CI [3.76, 6.60]), more than twice the figure in HIV–negative persons (2.16, 95% CI [1.65, 2.84]), and rose with age from 1.96 (95% CI [1.52, 2.77]) at 15–24 years to 3.34 (95% CI [2.27, 4.46]) at 45–64 years. Among individuals experiencing homelessness it was 1.87 percentage points (95% CI [0.14, 3.47]), and among the small group with drug-resistant tuberculosis, 8.77 percentage points (95% CI [1.46, 14.52]).

LTFU during tuberculosis treatment raised standardized 5-year mortality by 2.49 percentage points, and the excess was concentrated in tuberculosis-attributable deaths. 5-year risk differences were similar for disengagement at any point during the first 4 months of treatment, attenuating thereafter. The relative effects of LTFU were largest among younger, stably housed individuals, in whom the competing-mortality baseline is low, whereas on the absolute scale the greatest LTFU-attributable mortality burden fell on PLHIV. These findings, in a setting with high DOT coverage, point to the need for more effective models of care engagement throughout the course of treatment, particularly among PLHIV.

Brussels – It will cover the entire “life cycle of sanctions.” From their definition through to implementation, including awareness-raising activities, measures to combat circumvention and dialogue with third countries. Today (18 November), the European Commission established the EU Sanctions Office, to bring together expertise from the Berlaymont Building and work on all aspects of restrictive measures. The new approach aims to ensure the coordination of EU sanctions vis-à-vis Member States and third countries and covers all sanction regimes. These include Russia and Belarus, as well as Iran, North Korea, Syria, organised crime and hybrid threats. According to a press release, the Office will provide support to Member States through faster guidance “on compliance, data sharing, and economic and technical analysis, with a view to ensuring the harmonised implementation and enforcement of sanctions within the Union.” The European Commissioner for Financial Services and the Savings and Investment Union, Maria Luís Albuquerque, welcomed the establishment of the Office, announcing that “the Office will strengthen coordination within the Commission, bringing together expertise from different policy areas to ensure a more coherent approach to sanctions, wherever and whenever the need arises.”
For Brussels, the role of sanctions has been redefined by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the EU’s subsequent response. Specifically, sanctions have become “a foreign policy tool and a key means of addressing major international challenges.” Since the start of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, the EU has adopted 21 rounds of sanctions; however, for the measures “to be effective, they must be fully implemented, rigorously enforced and protected against any attempts to circumvent them,” stated the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen.
The new unit will be established within the General Secretariat at the Berlaymont Building and will operate under the political responsibility of Albuquerque. A central aspect of its work will be “to support the EU Sanctions Envoy, a key figure in the Union’s efforts to prevent the circumvention of restrictive measures and to cooperate with partner countries.” This role involves liaising with third countries to reduce the risk of EU sanctions being circumvented, for example through alternative trade routes, financial channels, or supply chains. For this role, the European Commission today appointed the Swedish diplomat, Lars Danielsson, who will take up the post on 6 February 2027, following the end of the current Envoy’s term of office, David O’Sullivan. In the past, Danielsson held senior positions in the Swedish Prime Minister’s Office, including that of State Secretary for International and EU Affairs, while from 2016 to 2023, he also served as Sweden’s Ambassador and Permanent Representative to the EU. All the changes announced today will come into effect on 16 January 2027.
European sources who have worked on the initiative have explained that, since “Russia is one of the countries most heavily affected by sanctions in the world, and the sanctions regime against Iran (which has been fully reinstated) is also one of the most extensive, it was necessary to develop a completely new working system to prepare, define, monitor, and implement the packages.” An EU official pointed out that in the current geopolitical landscape, “for sanctions to be effective, a strategic approach is first and foremost required which, by drawing on intelligence, enables an adversary’s weaknesses to be identified”. Secondly, “analytical capacity is required to understand supply chains and the various economic sectors.” Thirdly, “access to intelligence and consistency across different policies are necessary.” Finally, “the capacity to manage the implementation and enforcement of the measures is required.” He noted that “at present, this task is entrusted to individual Member States, with highly inconsistent results that create conditions of inequality, gaps and loopholes in the system”. The official pointed out that “at present, activities relating to sanctions are divided between the Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and the Capital Markets Union (DG FISMA), the Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security (DG TRADE), the Office of the Special Envoy and the General Secretariat.” The optimal solution “is to bring all these functions together within a single office,” which will become “solely responsible for drafting new measures,” following the College of Commissioners’ decision to “establish this office as a body with a high degree of autonomy,” he concluded.

- What’s new: BIS issued an interim final rule establishing new licensing requirements for advanced GPUs supplied to overseas data centers serving China and other restricted-country customers. The interim final rule also expands controls over shipments of advanced GPUs to all end users in five additional countries, tightens semiconductor manufacturing requirements and formally rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule.
- Why it matters: The rule expands restrictions on advanced computing infrastructure related to AI worldwide, creating significant know-your-customer obligations for shipments of covered GPUs to data centers. The rule also creates new licensing requirements for shipments of GPUs to countries suspected of diversion. Exporters and data center operators face heightened customer due diligence expectations.
- What to do next: Companies should consider assessing their exposure to the new licensing requirements, reviewing customer ownership and computing allocations, and determining whether existing operations require authorization within 90 days.
__________
Background
On November 16, 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule (IFR) titled “Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors,” marking the Trump administration’s most significant efforts to date to regulate exports of artificial intelligence (AI)-related technology. The IFR is scheduled to take effect upon publication in the Federal Register, expected on November 19, 2026. Public comments are due 60 days after publication.
Summary of the New Requirements
Prior to the IFR, U.S. export controls required licenses for exports, reexports and transfers (in-country) of advanced graphics processing unit (GPU) semiconductors and computers containing those GPUs (a) to approximately 40 countries worldwide (the Covered Countries) and, (b) on a global basis, for companies headquartered (or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered) in China, other Group D:5 Countries and Macau (together, the Prohibited Countries). The IFR adds five new jurisdictions to the list of Covered Countries and imposes additional global restrictions for data centers providing GPU access to users headquartered in Prohibited Countries. These changes expand licensing requirements and heighten customer due diligence expectations, and they will require companies to reassess existing customer relationships and computing arrangements. The IFR also formally rescinds the Biden administration’s AI Diffusion Rule, which BIS announced in May 2025 it would not enforce.
Access-based controls for overseas data centers. New Section 744.24 of the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR) establishes a worldwide licensing requirement for exports, reexports and transfers of covered advanced GPUs where there is “knowledge” that the items are destined for data centers providing or intending to provide “significant volumes” of compute access — more than 12 million “aggregate TPP” (i.e., total processing performance) — to or for companies headquartered (or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered) in Prohibited Countries. The threshold encompasses direct and indirect access, whether at one data center or through “linked data centers,” including digitally linked facilities. License applications will be reviewed on “a case-by-case basis,” meaning that BIS will be open to issuing licenses.
Before supplying covered advanced GPUs to foreign data centers, exporters, reexporters and transferors are expected to obtain sufficient information about those data centers’ customers to determine whether a license requirement is triggered based on direct or indirect ownership or control relationships by persons connected to the Prohibited Countries. If a foreign data center declines or is unable to provide information sufficient to verify compliance, the rule presumes “knowledge” that a licensing requirement is triggered for the advanced GPU supplier. Data centers already providing significant computing power to covered companies before the effective date of the IFR must obtain licenses from BIS within 90 days to continue providing those services or face “future export restrictions.” The licensing requirement does not apply where computing power is provided only for a “commercial recommender system” and specified information is submitted to BIS, an exception that may benefit some social media and e-commerce platform companies that would otherwise be impacted by the rule.
New license requirement for diversion-risk destinations. The IFR imposes a new license requirement for shipments of advanced GPUs to or within Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which BIS describes as presenting “a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.” With this change, a license is now required for shipments of covered GPUs to approximately 45 Covered Countries, regardless of the end user, and it applies in addition to the new global data center control. The requirement does not apply for the five newly added Covered Countries when the ultimate consignee or end user is headquartered (or has an ultimate parent company headquartered) in the U.S., provided that certain reporting requirements are met.
Semiconductor manufacturing. The rule narrows existing pathways for front-end fabricators and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) companies to rebut the presumption that certain advanced-node logic chips, including applicable advanced logic integrated circuits, are classified under ECCN 3A090.a1 when their designers are located (or have ultimate parents headquartered) in Country Groups D:1, D:4 or D:5 or the five newly covered countries. It also establishes a worldwide licensing requirement for exports, reexports or transfers by these manufacturers of covered chips subject to the EAR and classified under ECCN 3A090.a when the designer is neither an Approved nor Authorized IC Designer.
AI Diffusion Rule. The rule formally rescinds the Biden administration’s AI Diffusion Rule, including its country-tier framework for shipments of advanced GPUs, its controls on AI model weights, and related license exceptions and authorizations. Because BIS had already announced that it would not enforce that rule, the rescission largely formalizes the existing position and clarifies the EAR provisions that remain applicable.
Treatment of the UAE. The rule preserves the United Arab Emirates’ (UAE’s) favorable treatment under BIS’s July 2026 amendments to its country groups. Most transfers of covered advanced GPUs to or within the UAE require licenses, with applications reviewed under a presumption of approval. This license requirement does not apply where the ultimate consignee and all end users are listed in Supplement No. 8 to Part 740 and approved to receive covered items without a license.2
Open Questions and Next Steps
The rule leaves several key questions unresolved, including the factors to be considered by BIS in reviewing data center license applications on a “case-by-case” basis, the specifics of the “commercial recommender system” exception and the consequences for data centers that apply for but do not receive licenses within the IFR’s 90-day window. Companies should consider raising these issues during the 60-day comment period.
______________
1 Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) 3A090.a covers certain advanced computing integrated circuits, including high-performance GPUs, that meet specified thresholds for total processing performance and performance density under the EAR.
2 The UAE also benefits from expanded license exception eligibility under the July amendments, including License Exception Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for eligible items destined for entities specifically approved to use that exception. These authorizations do not override applicable Part 744 end-use and end-user restrictions, including the new data center controls.

Le Système solaire est plus grand qu'on ne le pense. Sa frontière est généralement établie dans une région que les astronomes nomment le nuage d'Oort. Il s'agit d'un vaste amas de planétésimaux (restes de planètes comme des astéroïdes ou comètes), étendu sur 2 000 à 100 000 unités astronomiques, soit l'équivalent de 2 000 à 100 000 fois la distance entre la Terre et le Soleil.
Alors que la plupart des sondes explorent des planètes telles que Mercure, Vénus ou Mars, seule une poignée se sont aventurées au-delà de Pluton : New Horizons, Voyager 1 et Voyager 2.
Le programme Voyager est un cas singulier. La mission spatiale de la Nasa, lancée officiellement le 20 août avec Voyager 2, suivie de Voyager 1 le 5 septembre 1977, demeure la seule à avoir dépassé l'héliosphère. Cette dernière correspond à une gigantesque bulle protectrice de particules et de champs magnétiques générée par notre étoile qui entoure notre système solaire. Voyager 1 et 2 ont été ainsi conçues comme des messagers interstellaires.

ANTALYA, Turkey—The science that guides negotiators and policymakers at the United Nations’ COP31 climate change conference is “under a serious and highly politicized attack,” said Laurence Tubiana, a veteran French climate diplomat and one of the architects of the 2015 Paris climate agreement.
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, established in 1988 to inform international climate negotiations, regularly assesses thousands of studies on rising temperatures, sea level rise, melting ice and strategies for adapting to the increasingly intense impacts of global warming.
But three countries—Russia and Saudi Arabia, both major fossil fuel producers, and India, which accounts for an estimated 14 percent of global coal consumption—are blocking progress on future reports, according to scientists on the panel and independent observers.
Those countries “are doing everything they can to slow the process,” Tubiana said. They are becoming less discreet about their efforts, she said, as they increasingly view their economies as threatened by a conditional agreement to transition away from coal, oil and gas reached during COP28, the 2023 Conference of the Parties conference in Dubai.
The science panel’s current impasse is especially troubling, “because we know climate problems are accelerating, and we need a lot of data and communication to understand what’s happening at this COP,” said Mary Robinson, former president of Ireland and former United Nations special envoy on climate change.
Robinson said this isn’t the first time countries have tried to obstruct science. Recent examples include attacks seeking to undermine a recent United Nations Environment Programme report on “overshoot,” which concludes that there is no way to avoid passing the 2.7 degree Fahrenheit warming target in the Paris Agreement.
Fossil fuels account for an estimated 80 percent to 90 percent of planet-heating carbon dioxide emissions, according to the IPCC’s 2023 assessment.
The international climate science panel relies on voluntary donations from member countries to fund its work, including periodic assessments, some of which inform steps required under the Paris Agreement. The panel has yet to set a budget for next year, potentially delaying a scientific report needed ahead of next year’s U.N. climate conference.
“Since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the oil and gas sector has become much more aggressive,” Tubiana said. “I think this is partly because it sees its dominance over energy starting to erode.”
Oil and gas companies are losing ground in transport as electric-vehicle adoption in Asia surges faster than expected, she said, adding that reports from the International Energy Agency show demand for fossil fuels is set to slow.
“Investors hear the message that the decline is coming, and those governments have pushed back,” she said.

The 2023 IPCC report concluded that existing and planned fossil fuel infrastructure would push global warming beyond the Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming as close as possible to 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average.
Tubiana said a growing number of countries view the transition away from fossil fuels as a path to greater energy independence and security, while those opposed to the shift are becoming “more angry and vocal.”
“The danger,” she said, “is that they take other countries along with them that aren’t necessarily committed to that position.”
The latest draft of the conference’s decision document highlights the assessments’ importance to the negotiations. Some countries also want to include language that could help break the science panel’s deadlock, but the same countries stalling the IPCC are resisting that effort.
In particular, the climate, environment and energy ministers participating in the current round of talks could help the IPCC get over the political hurdles it faces, said Bill Hare, CEO of Climate Analytics, an international climate science and policy institute.
Hare said the countries participating in the U.N. talks should advocate for continued support for the IPCC. If the panel can’t deliver the needed climate science “because of political obstacles created by a small number of countries, it would be a historic setback for the connection between science and the international climate process.”
Robinson said some of the world’s least developed countries and small island states “desperately need” the international panel’s reports because they can’t do their own climate assessments.
“We need the authoritative, legitimate IPCC science, which has guided us from the beginning in this whole climate process,” she said. “It’s just a sign of the difficult times we’re in that we have to fight for it. I can hardly believe it.”

Jurassic Park, le retour ? Au début du mois de novembre, une actualité scientifique a fait le tour de la planète, dépassant largement le cercle de la paléontologie : des traces de sang de dinosaure auraient été retrouvées sur un fossile vieux de 115 millions d’années, conservé au Brésil, titrent des médias du monde entier.
Que des reliques biologiques d’un animal ayant vécu au Crétacé inférieur aient ainsi traversé les âges serait effectivement extraordinaire. Rappelons que, dans le film hollywoodien, les héros ressuscitent des dinosaures après avoir extrait leur ADN ancien d’échantillons sanguins conservés dans le corps de moustiques figés dans l’ambre. La réalité est évidemment un peu moins fantastique…
Une équipe internationale a effectivement réalisé une première : les chercheurs ont retrouvé des structures qui sont très vraisemblablement des globules rouges minéralisés à l’intérieur d’un fossile d’Aratasaurus, un petit représentant de la lignée des théropodes. "C’est convaincant, car c’est la première fois que l’on identifie formellement des globules rouges sur un fossile aussi ancien, grâce à un travail performant rendu possible par des instruments comme le laser ou le microscope électronique", résume Romain Amiot, paléobiologiste et directeur de recherche au CNRS (Laboratoire de géologie de Lyon, Terre, Planètes et Environnement).

L’ESSENTIEL
- Le terme « terres rares » désigne un ensemble de 17 éléments chimiques.
- Ils ont des propriétés très intéressantes pour de nombreuses applications industrielles, ils sont donc devenus des ressources stratégiques majeures.
- La Chine est l’un des acteurs majeurs du domaine mais la France a également des atouts.
Qualifiées de « vitamines de l’ère moderne » en raison de leurs propriétés catalytiques, optiques, magnétiques et électroniques exceptionnelles, les terres rares présentent un intérêt stratégique pour de nombreuses technologies actuelles, dans les secteurs de l’énergie bas carbone, de la défense, de l’électronique (écrans LCD, LED, composants de disques durs et de smartphones) et du médical (IRM, lasers). Le secteur le plus important est celui des aimants permanents, surtout néodyme-fer-bore (NdFeB), pour les moteurs des véhicules électriques ou les équipements des éoliennes. Les autres secteurs, comme les catalyseurs pour l’automobile, les poudres de polissage ou les alliages nécessitent des terres rares plus abondantes et moins coûteuses que le néodyme, surtout le lanthane et le cérium.
Ainsi, la plus forte demande concerne le néodyme (près du tiers du total), suivi du cérium, du lanthane, du praséodyme et de l’yttrium, les autres terres rares représentant environ 5 % de la demande.
La Chine comme principal acteur
Selon l’Union européenne, la production mondiale était de 278 000 tonnes de concentrés d’oxydes de terres rares en 2021, soit plus du double de celle de 2010 (129 000 tonnes). Le marché est faible par rapport à des métaux très répandus comme le fer (2 500 millions de tonnes en 2023) mais très supérieur à des métaux rares comme le platine (183 000 tonnes en 2022). La production est dominée par la Chine, avec près de 60 % en 2021, et environ 70 % de l’extraction mondiale en 2023 – une domination qui s’étend plus largement encore au raffinage et à la séparation, où la Chine concentre 85 à 90 % des capacités mondiales. Cette situation lui confère le pouvoir de diminuer l’approvisionnement, comme cela s’est produit en 2011, voire de le couper. Aussi, les États-Unis, l’Australie, le Canada et les pays d’Europe cherchent à diversifier leur production pour réduire leur dépendance. Les États-Unis ont rouvert en 2018 la mine de Mountain Pass en Californie, et visent de nouvelles ressources, notamment au Groenland, qui possèdent un stock important mais difficilement exploitable.
Mais que sont exactement les terres rares, et pourquoi sont-elles si difficiles à extraire ? Le terme « terres rares » désigne un ensemble de 17 éléments chimiques, comprenant 15 lanthanides (du lanthane 57La au lutétium 71Lu) ainsi que le scandium (21Sc) et l’yttrium (39Y). Ce ne sont pas des « terres » et elles ne sont pas « rares », mais relativement abondantes dans la croûte terrestre.
Ces éléments se trouvent dans différents minéraux porteurs, principalement la bastnaésite, la monazite et le xénotime, qui contiennent aussi des éléments radioactifs. Leur extraction est complexe et coûteuse.
En les classant selon leur masse atomique, on distingue les terres rares légères : lanthane, cérium, praséodyme, néodyme, et samarium des terres rares lourdes : europium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, holmium, erbium, thulium, ytterbium, lutécium et yttrium. N’entrent pas dans cette classification le prométhium, élément instable, ni le scandium. Les légères sont plus abondantes et plus facilement extractibles que les lourdes, qui sont, elles, plus stratégiques. Elles sont toutes répertoriées dans la liste des métaux critiques et stratégiques de la Commission européenne.
Comment produit-on les terres rares ?
La production de terres rares commence par la prospection et l’exploitation minière, puis implique des traitements chimiques pour séparer ces éléments dont les propriétés sont proches. Elle se termine par l’affinage et la purification pour obtenir des composés possédant les spécificités requises pour les différentes applications. En France, l’usine Solvay à La Rochelle, mise en service en 1948, possède un savoir-faire historique en séparation et purification, qui en fait aujourd’hui le seul site européen à traiter l’ensemble des terres rares en quantité.
Actuellement, moins de 1 % des terres rares est recyclé. Le recyclage est difficile car ces éléments se trouvent souvent dans des structures complexes et des alliages. Des efforts sont faits en ce sens ; une usine de recyclage d’aimants et de raffinage de concentrés miniers de la société Caremag, filiale de Carester, est en construction près de Lacq (Pyrénées-Atlantiques) ; elle vise à produire environ 600 tonnes d’oxydes de terres rares lourdes (dysprosium, terbium), soit environ 15 % de la production mondiale actuelle de ces éléments, par raffinage (5 000 tonnes de concentrés par an) et par recyclage (2000 tonnes d’aimants par an). Un protocole d’accord a été signé entre Carester et Solvay en 2024 en vue de créer un partenariat stratégique.
On connaît bien aujourd’hui les impacts environnementaux des terres rares, dont l’exploitation contribue à la destruction des écosystèmes, à la contamination des sols et des eaux et à la production de déchets toxiques. Leur utilisation n’est pas non plus sans effet, par exemple, le gadolinium utilisé comme agent de contraste en IRM se retrouve dans les cours d’eau. La toxicité des terres, encore mal connue, fait l’objet de nombreuses recherches. Les terres rares, bien qu’elles aient pu être utilisées comme engrais, affectent la croissance des plantes ; néanmoins, certaines peuvent être phytoextraites et valorisées par agromine. L’agromine combine la phytoextraction, ici de terres rares, à partir de plantes capables de les accumuler et le traitement des tissus des plantes pour récupérer ces éléments d’intérêt.

depeches.resume: NSN a annoncé, ce mercredi, la signature de Primoz Roglic pour la saison 2027. Le Slovène, quadruple vainqueur du Tour d'Espagne, était sans équipe après la fin de son contrat chez Red Bull - Bora-Hansgrohe.

depeches.titre: La Classic Loire-Atlantique annulée en 2027
depeches.resume: Déjà annulée en 2025 pour des contraintes financières puis relancée cette année, la Classic Loire-Atlantique va être annulée la saison prochaine, handicapée par la perte de subventions.

depeches.resume: Championnat de France de rugby à 7, le Supersevens va connaître plusieurs changements en vue de la saison 2027-2028. La LNR et la FFR prévoient l'organisation de détections de joueurs amateurs ainsi qu'un changement de calendrier.

depeches.resume: La LNR a communiqué ce mercredi les moyennes intermédiaires de JIFF par club, calculées après 7 journées de Top 14, cette saison. depeches.resume: INFO L'ÉQUIPE. Louis Bielle-Biarrey et Jean-Baptiste Gros, ménagés ce mercredi midi à Marcoussis, seront bien titulaires pour la réception de l'Argentine samedi soir (21h10) dans le Championnat des nations.

Bielle-Biarrey et Gros ménagés à l'entraînement, le reste de la compo du XV de France face à l'Argentine se confirme

depeches.resume: La performance d'Antoine Dupont avec le XV de France contre l'Afrique du Sud vendredi (21-19) a épaté les observateurs étrangers qui crient de nouveau au génie.

depeches.resume: Moins souverain lors du printemps, alors qu'il reprenait la compétition après son opération à un genou, le capitaine de l'équipe de France Antoine Dupont a retrouvé tout son potentiel physique, et donc une part de son génie, depuis quelques semaines.

depeches.resume: En raison de conclusions peu convaincantes après une phase de test conduite dans le Championnat canadien depuis début avril, le projet de loi Wenger sur le hors-jeu devrait être abandonné par la FIFA d'après le « New York Times ». Arsène Wenger lui-même n'aurait pas été convaincu.

depeches.resume: Malgré sa défaite en Italie (1-3), l'équipe de France termine l'année à la troisième position du classement FIFA. Derrière, le Maroc intègre le top 5, laissant le Brésil dans son rétroviseur.

depeches.resume: Claude Le Roy a annoncé mardi après la défaite face aux Comores (0-1) qu'il allait quitter son poste de sélectionneur du Congo. Une déception immense pour l'entraîneur de 78 ans, qui dit avoir « failli » à sa mission, liée à une qualification à la CAN 2027.

depeches.resume: Selon « El Pais », la Fédération espagnole de football (RFEF) aurait décelé des manoeuvres de certains proches de Luis Rubiales pour tenter de renverser le président Rafael Louzan. depeches.resume: Titulaire presque indiscutable avec le Real Madrid depuis l'arrivée de José Mourinho, Arda Güler a prolongé son contrat avec le club merengue ce mercredi. L'international turc est désormais lié à la Maison Blanche jusqu'en 2032.

La prise de position du Paris Basketball pour promouvoir la diversité du XVIIIe arrondissement
depeches.resume: Dans une vidéo publiée mercredi sur ses réseaux sociaux, le Paris Basketball a réagi à des propos tenus par la journaliste Christine Kelly sur Europe 1 au sujet d'un soi-disant « racisme anti-blanc » qui sévirait dans le XVIIIe arrondissement de la capitale, où se situe l'Adidas Arena.

depeches.titre: Malgré un grand Théo Maledon, le Real Madrid surpris par Besiktas en Euroligue
depeches.resume: Dans le cadre de la 12e journée d'Euroligue, le Real Madrid s'est incliné sur le parquet du Besiktas, ce mercredi (83-79). Le meneur français Théo Maledon a quand même inscrit 22 points.

depeches.titre: Malgré la guerre, la vie comme avant à Dubaï
La Cour des comptes publie sa première note de synthèse sur les « financements publics dédiés au sport » afin de « nourrir le débat public »
depeches.resume: La Cour des comptes publie jeudi sa première note de synthèse sur « les financements publics dédiés au sport », estimés à 17 Mds€, et rappelle les priorités dans un « contexte budgétaire tendu ».

depeches.titre: La Cour des comptes clôt les comptes de Paris 2024 à 6,6 milliards d'euros d'argent public
depeches.resume: La Cour des comptes publiera jeudi son dernier bilan des Jeux de Paris 2024, qui ont coûté 6,6 Mds€ d'argent public, et adresse ses recommandations aux Alpes 2030.

depeches.titre: Audrey Zarif et Joé Seyfried au deuxième tour du Star Contender de Mascate
depeches.resume: Audrey Zarif et Joé Seyfried se sont qualifiés ce mercredi pour les 16es de finale du Star Contender de Mascate, à Oman. Ça ne passe pas en revanche pour Charlotte Lutz.

depeches.titre: Rastafari, millionnaire et GOAT du skate : rencontre avec Nyjah Huston
depeches.resume: Il ne fait pas l'unanimité quand il s'agit de son style, de ses propos ou de son mode de vie. Mais Nyjah Huston reste le GOAT du skate. Nous avons pu le rencontrer, à Paris. À presque 32 ans, le skateur américain continue d'impressionner dans un sport d'ultra jeunes. Élevé dans la tradition rastafar

depeches.titre: "Fais grève pendant 15 jours": l'appel de Rothen à Mbappé pour renverser Infantino
depeches.resume: Jérôme Rothen appelle à une mobilisation massive des joueurs et notamment des stars internationales pour mettre fin au règne de Gianni Infantino à la tête de la Fifa.

depeches.titre: Ligue des champions féminine: le PSG a fini par craquer à Chelsea
depeches.resume: Les féminines du Paris Saint-Germain ont résisté aux vagues bleues de Chelsea pendant longtemps mercredi à Londres, avant de craquer sur le tard sur un but évitable qui les place aux portes de l'élimination en Ligue des champions.

depeches.titre: Manchester United prêt à aller en justice après le départ de sa pépite JJ Gabriel, vers le Real Madrid
depeches.resume: Passablement agacé par le départ de JJ Gabriel, ce grand espoir anglais de 19 ans en passe de signer au Real Madrid, Manchester United pourrait se lancer dans une bataille juridique.

depeches.titre: Le violent tacle du directeur sportif de Nice sur le départ de Sage de Lens
depeches.resume: Invité à réagir au départ de Pierre Sage l'été dernier après une saison plus que réussie à Lens, le directeur sportif de Nice, Roger Ricort, a déploré une situation "insupportable", qui met à mal la notion d'"identité" des clubs de football modernes.

depeches.titre: Monaco: comme Paris Bunner, Mamadou Coulibaly suspendu après sa célébration polémique
depeches.resume: Après son coéquipier Paris Brunner, Mamadou Coulibaly avait à son tour célébré un but de Monaco en mimant un tranchage de gorge. Un geste qui lui vaut d'être sanctionné par la commission de discipline de la LFP.

depeches.titre: Real Madrid: "Je dois lui demander de faire mon travail?", Rüdiger défend Mbappé sur les replis défensifs
depeches.resume: Dans une interview accordée à The Athletic, Antonio Rüdiger a balayé d'un revers de la main les critiques visant l'implication défensive de Kylian Mbappé. D'après le défenseur allemand, personne n'aurait demandé cela à l'époque de Karim Benzema, Gareth Bale et Cristiano Ronaldo.

depeches.titre: Tennis: Zverev visé par une nouvelle plainte de son ex-compagne
depeches.resume: Le N.1 mondial Alexander Zverev, actuellement en lice au Masters ATP à Turin, fait face à une nouvelle plainte de son ex-compagne qui lui reproche des propos publics liés au règlement amiable du procès qu'elle lui avait intenté pour coups et blessures.

depeches.titre: Strasbourg: Oliveira quitte le club, Matos le remplace
depeches.resume: Après avoir annoncé le départ d'Hugo Oliveira, Strasbourg a officialisé ce mercredi l'arrivée de son nouveau coach Vitor Matos. Arrivé de Swansea, le Portugais de 38 ans devient le quatrième entraîneur à s'asseoir sur le banc alsacien en 2026.

depeches.titre: OL: DNCG à venir, mercato hivernal... des finances toujours fragiles mais en nette amélioration
depeches.resume: Michele Kang a affiché ce mercredi un optimisme résolu et volontariste, même si elle demande, encore de la patience à ses supporters en détaillant sa méthode mêlant rigueur financière, travail sans modération et résultats constants à haute altitude en Ligue 1. depeches.titre: "Une solution de secours": pourquoi Clauss croit encore à l'équipe de France
depeches.resume: Artisan majeur du bon début de saison réussi par l'OGC Nice, Jonathan Clauss se verrait bien revenir en équipe de France, alors qu'il était absent des deux premiers rassemblements de Zinédine Zidane.

depeches.titre: Ligue 1: sonorisation des arbitres à améliorer, hors-jeu semi-automatique... dans les coulisses de la VAR, qui cherche à faire l'unanimité
depeches.resume: C'est dans une adresse tenue secrète que la Direction de l'arbitrage (DA) a accueilli RMC Sport pour une séance d'initiation à la VAR. Un exercice que la DA met en place dans une démarche pédagogique. Dans une grande salle remplie d'écrans, des arbitres et opérateurs revisionnent des milliers d'imag

depeches.titre: Pas encore de retraite: Primoz Roglic annonce sa nouvelle équipe pour 2027
depeches.resume: Le Slovène Primoz Roglic (37 ans), quadruple vainqueur du Tour d'Espagne, a signé avec les Suisses de NSN Cycling pour la saison prochaine.

depeches.titre: La France doit-elle encore candidater pour accueillir des événements sportifs après les coûteux JO 2024?
depeches.resume: La Cour des comptes vient de publier son rapport sur le bilan financier et l’héritage des Jeux olympiques et paralympiques de Paris 2024. À quelques mois de l’élection présidentielle, l’institution alerte sur les dépenses publiques liées à l’organisation d’événements sportifs.

depeches.titre: La France toujours sur le podium, le Maroc à une place historique... le nouveau classement Fifa a été révélé
depeches.resume: Après les rencontres internationales de novembre, la Fifa a mis à jour son fameux classement des nations. Si l'Espagne reste en tête, deux mouvements sont à noter dans le Top 10.

depeches.titre: Afrique du Sud: suspendu et interdit de stade, Rassie Erasmus organise une watch party du prochain match des Boks et vous êtes tous invités
depeches.resume: Suspendu après ses propos polémiques contre l'arbitrage de France-Afrique du Sud (21-19), Rassie Erasmus ne pourra pas assister au match des Springboks contre l'Irlande ce samedi (17h40). Mais, toujours aussi provocateur, le sélectionneur a proposé aux internautes de le voir réagir en direct à la re

depeches.titre: Congo: Claude Le Roy démissionne de la sélection après quatre matchs
depeches.resume: Revenu en juin dernier sur le banc du Congo, avec comme objectif la qualification pour la CAN 2027, Claude Le Roy (78 ans) a annoncé sa démission mardi.

depeches.titre: OM: Hojbjerg, Paixao... pourquoi les dossiers de l'été pourraient aussi agiter le mercato de janvier
depeches.resume: La vente d'un joueur pourrait être un élément clé du redressement financier de l'OM, à la fois pour passer l'obstacle DNCG et pouvoir recruter en janvier. Les cas emblématiques de Hojbjerg et Paixao ont évolué depuis cet été, et seront à surveiller.

depeches.titre: OL: "Le stade doit être un lieu sûr et sacré pour tous", affirme Michele Kang après les polémiques de racisme autour du club
depeches.resume: Lors d'une conférence de presse qui s'est tenue ce mercredi à Lyon, Michele Kang a rappelé condamner toutes formes de violence lors des matchs de l'OL au Groupama Stadium.

depeches.titre: "On verra très vite qui a des cernes": GTA 6 va-t-il vraiment plomber les performances des sportifs?
depeches.resume: Enfin disponible ce jeudi à minuit au bout d’une interminable attente, le sixième opus de la mythique saga Grand Theft Auto se tient prêt à tout écraser sur son passage. Peut-être même à dérégler le monde du sport. Certains s’inquiètent déjà d’une prochaine baisse des performances avec des joueurs p

depeches.titre: Diallo candidat à la présidence de la Fifa: le candidat japonais Tashima "souhaite avoir une discussion" avec le Français
depeches.resume: Deux jours après l'officialisation de la candidature de Philippe Diallo à la présidence de la Fifa, le candidat japonais a fait un pas en avant vers le patron de la FFF. Les deux hommes, "totalement alignés" sur le plan des idées, vont rapidement échanger.

depeches.titre: La folle vidéo de présentation de JJ Gabriel, le "Neymar du futur" annoncé au Real Madrid, chez son nouvel agent
depeches.resume: Annoncé comme un joueur doté d’un potentiel incroyable, Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill dit "JJ Gabriel" pourrait rapidement quitter Manchester United pour le Real Madrid. Mais avant de signer en Espagne, l’attaquant de 16 ans a été présenté en grande pompe par son nouvel agent.

depeches.titre: France-Argentine: pourquoi Gourgues, un joueur qui n’a buté qu’une fois chez les pros, butera contre les Pumas
depeches.resume: Kalvin Gourgues sera chargé du jeu au pied du XV de France ce samedi lors du match du Championnat des nations contre l’Argentine. Le centre du Stade Toulousain, pas habitué de l’exercice chez les pros, a pourtant vu le staff des Bleus lui confier cette grosse responsabilité face aux Pumas.

depeches.titre: PSG: Marquinhos, un retour imminent et une prolongation d’un an à l’étude
depeches.resume: Alors qu'il pourrait faire son retour dès ce week-end en Ligue 1, Marquinhos s'est vu offrir une prolongation d'un an par le PSG. Des discussions sont en cours.

depeches.titre: Didier Deschamps va faire son retour... dans une publicité pour Burger King
depeches.resume: Depuis son départ de l'équipe de France à l'issue de la Coupe du monde 2026, Didier Deschamps se faisait discret. Mais d'après les informations de RMC Sport, l'ancien sélectionneur des Bleus va refaire son apparition à l'écran dans une publicité pour Burger King lors de la mi-temps du match de rugby

depeches.titre: Une autre danse pour Ronaldinho en Série C? L'entraîneur de Ravenne ouvre la porte à un autre match avec la star brésilienne
depeches.resume: Après le retour inattendu de Ronaldinho sur un terrain de football, samedi dernier avec le club de Ravenne (D3 italienne), l'entraîneur de l'équipe est revenu sur le match disputé par le Brésilien. Et il n'exclut pas qu'il rejoue une autre rencontre cette saison.

depeches.titre: France-Afrique du Sud: "Ça aurait pu être bien plus grave", Gourgues très cash après le geste dangereux de Wiese
depeches.resume: Quelques jours après la victoire face à l’Afrique du Sud, le trois-quarts centre Kalvin Gourgues n’a pas hésité à souligner la dangerosité du déblayage du troisième ligne centre Jasper Wiese, lequel vient d’être suspendu.

depeches.titre: "Un potentiel hors-norme qu’il ne faut pas griller": pourquoi Abdellah Ouazane, 17 ans, suscite un tel engouement au Maroc
depeches.resume: Alors qu’il n’est pas encore majeur, Abdellah Ouazane s’est montré décisif dès sa première titularisation avec le Maroc en offrant la victoire face au Niger, mardi à Rabat (1-0). Une réalisation synonyme de qualification pour la CAN 2027, qui lui a permis de devenir le plus jeune buteur de l’histoir

depeches.titre: La championne olympique de boxe Estelle Mossely s'engage dans la campagne présidentielle d'Edouard Philippe
depeches.resume: Première boxeuse française à avoir remporté un titre olympique, lors des Jeux de Rio en 2016, Estelle Mossely fait partie de l'équipe de campagne d'Édouard Philippe, président du parti Horizons et candidat à l'élection présidentielle de 2027.
